1bd60923b8e7a6b8: SRINAGAR, Sept 24 — Residents in India’s Ladakh staged a virtual shutdown of the main city today to mark a year since four people were killed during a protest for greater regional autonomy.
On September 24, 2025, security forces opened fire as demonstrations turned violent in the sparsely populated, high-altitude Himalayan region.
The discontent stems from a decision by the Indian government in 2019 to cancel Ladakh’s partial automony and impose direct rule.
Shops and businesses in the city of Leh remained shut and streets were deserted on Thursday, witnesses said, in response to calls for their closure by a Buddhist group.

“The shutdown is to commemorate those who laid down their lives for Ladakh and express solidarity with their families, and... to highlight our demands for autonomy,” a member of the Ladakh Buddhist Association told AFP, declining to be named.
Residents organised special Buddhist prayers to commemorate what they called the “martyrs” of the protests.
Ladakh is strategically important for India as it borders regional rivals China and Pakistan.
The vast desert region is sparsely populated by some 300,000 people, half of them Muslim and about 40 percent Buddhist.

Since Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government split Ladakh from Indian-administered Kashmir in 2019, residents have said the end of semi-autonomy has stripped them of protections over land, jobs, resources and cultural identity.
New Delhi now makes most decisions on development, and officials from outside Ladakh tend to impelement them, sidelining the local elected council.
On Wednesday, the New Delhi-appointed top administrator of Ladakh said some of the 89 people charged after last year’s protests would no longer face criminal prosections.

“In the larger interest of peace, public tranquility, and social harmony in Ladakh, I have approved the withdrawal of criminal cases against 20 individuals, related to the unfortunate violence that erupted in Leh on September 24 last year,” Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena said.
“The decision aims at fostering a more peaceful, united, and harmonious society in Ladakh.”
Negotiations with the federal home ministry have been going on since the protests, but local people have only secured some small gains so far.
The government has reserved 85 percent of jobs for locals and said Indians from outside Ladakh will not be able to acquire domicile status in the region until 2036.

But residents are demanding comprehensive autonomy under the “Sixth Schedule” of India’s constitution, which would allow a local legislature to make laws on land use, jobs and traditional livelihoods. — AFP
603ea416ae97c931: TOKYO, Sept 24 — Japanese teenager Shin Ohashi smashed the men’s 200m breaststroke world record in winning gold at the Asian Games on Thursday, setting a new mark of 2min 04.83sec.
The 17-year-old cut more than half a second off the previous mark of 2:05.48 held by China’s Qin Haiyang.
Qin’s record had stood since July 2023.
Ohashi had already won the 100m breaststroke gold this week in Tokyo after a dead heat with China’s Dong Zhihao.
“My target has always been to break the world record and I’m so happy to have done it,” said Ohashi.
“A lot happened before this competition but a lot of people helped me get to this point and I am very grateful to them.
Ohashi finished 3.84sec faster than silver medallist Denis Petrashov of Kyrgyzstan.
The Japanese teen took control from the off and from then it was a race against the clock.
He will now be the man to beat at the Los Angeles Olympics in two years’ time.
“My next goal is to win gold at next year’s world championships and then go on to win gold at the Olympics,” he said.
“I don’t want to be satisfied and I want to feel these emotions again.”
Previous world record holder Qin did not swim the 200m at this year’s Asian Games. — AFP
913baae9fb251755: KUALA LUMPUR: The government must introduce bold policy shifts in the 2027 Budget to address brain drain in the high-tech sector and retain Malaysia's semiconductor talent, said a student of International Affairs at Ming Chuan University in Taipei.
Farid Maulud said the exodus of local engineering and technology talent represented a direct challenge to Malaysia's economic sovereignty.
He said as the government prepares the 2027 Budget, its policy focus must move beyond raw investment figures towards job quality and human capital retention.

"The core reality distinguishing Malaysia from regional tech hubs like South Korea, Singapore and Taiwan is not merely the presence of multinational giants, but how local engineers are valued through research and development (R&D) ecosystems," he said in a statement today.

Farid said according to data from the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) and the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), while manufacturing investments continued to grow, entry-level median salaries for engineering and technical graduates remained stagnant at between RM3,000 and RM4,500.
This, he said, was compounded by World Bank findings indicating that about 5.5 per cent of highly educated Malaysians migrate abroad, a rate well above the global average.

Farid said while Penang and the Klang Valley had long functioned as global hubs for outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) operations, an over-reliance on back-end processing left highly skilled professionals undercompensated.

"Without fertile ground for R&D, local engineering talent will continue to seek international markets that offer starting salaries ranging from RM8,000 to RM15,000 for integrated circuit (IC) design and intellectual property development roles," he said.
To transition Malaysia from an assembly hub into a high-income design and innovation economy, Farid said several key policy pillars should be included in the 2027 Budget.

"First, the government should offer equity and tax incentives for local R&D by encouraging strategic joint ventures and IP royalty-sharing structures, enabling local startups to offer competitive stock options and remuneration.

"Second, the National Semiconductor Strategy (NSS) must prioritise IC design-focused execution by allocating targeted funding for shared design infrastructure, such as Electronic Design Automation (EDA) software licence subsidies and Multi-Project Wafer (MPW) testing access for local firms in industrial hubs like Bayan Lepas and Batu Kawan.
"Finally, establishing dignified wages through competitive domestic compensation will preserve social harmony and prevent skilled professionals from having to relocate overseas."

He added that Malaysia possessed all the necessary infrastructure to serve as a strong, neutral regional tech hub, provided the 2027 Budget demonstrated the political will to realise the "Made by Malaysia" ambition.
f93d4ec9c2c646ed: KUALA LUMPUR: ​Last month, fans were left concerned when actress Jesseca Liu posted a photo of her husband, actor Jeremy Chan, using a walking stick.
​It turns out the 45-year-old actor had aggravated an old back injury so severely that he was left virtually immobile for two days.
The pain was so intense that standing, sitting, or lying down was nearly impossible—leaving him reliant on Liu, 47, for basic tasks like getting dressed.
​Chan revealed that his back troubles date back to 2023, while filming the Mediacorp blockbuster All That Glitters, where he played a Muay Thai boxer.
He occasionally strained his back during production whenever he skipped a proper warm-up.
A combination of those past strains, a lack of rest, and "getting on in years" finally caught up with him on a recent day off.
​Things took a turn for the worse when Chan drove himself to a traditional physician, only to find he could barely walk after receiving acupuncture.
Realising the severity of the situation, he called his wife to take him to a doctor, where he was given pain relief medication and a steroid injection.
​"For two days, I couldn't stand, sit, or lie down. Every movement had to be extremely slow," Chan recalled.
"Imagine if I had to rely on the film crew to help me change clothes. That would have been so embarrassing!" he added with a laugh.
​While Liu offered to join him on set as his assistant during his recovery, Chan declined, not wanting to put her out.
Fortunately, after three acupuncture sessions, his mobility improved enough for him to manage on his own.
​As for the walking stick that kicked off the fan concern? It wasn't originally bought for him.
​Chan explained that he had purchased a portable walking stick—one that unfolds into a small chair—for his mother-in-law, who suffers from leg pain when joining them on holiday.
​"Who knew that before she even got the chance to use it, I'd be the one breaking it in first?" he joked.
​Though Chan has yet to undergo a full medical examination, he confirmed he is currently on the mend.
The ordeal served as a strong reminder not to take his physical health for granted.
​"These days, I make it a point to stretch more—I even take my time getting out of bed in the morning instead of springing straight up."

611207117c8991d9: MariaDB has built vector search into its database. Its problem is persuading AI coding tools to tell anyone about it, says the executive chairman of the MariaDB Foundation. "We're so frustrated that the world doesn't understand that MariaDB has vectors," Kaj Arnö tells us. Arnö is speaking to The Register at Percona Live, where rival database vendors seem to be in an unusually collegiate mood. Not that Arnö is above throwing a little shade here and there: "I think we are in a period of calmness and sort of sailing smooth waters and seeing how AI impacts stuff, how extensibility impacts stuff… and I'm not as sure that MySQL is going through all that smooth times." MariaDB was forked from MySQL in 2009 as Oracle's acquisition of Sun Microsystems loomed. It now supports vector search, which lets applications find items by similarity rather than exact matches – a common requirement in AI applications. The nonprofit MariaDB Foundation supports development of the open source server and its community, while MariaDB plc develops the commercial products and provides support. MariaDB is familiar to users of many Linux distributions. Arnö's concern is whether developers starting a new AI project will ever be pointed toward it. "People start using vector databases based on some framework or based on some default choices of the LLM," he explains. "So if you do vibecoding and just sort of press enter when Claude Code suggests something, you will not end up using MariaDB for your vector search, and that is what we need to change." Arnö attributes part of the problem to the information available to AI tools. Their training data may predate MariaDB's vector features, while the documentation and examples developers encounter elsewhere may still favor established alternatives. "There are a million places where we need to update stuff so that the frameworks, the training data for the LLMs, and all of those know about the existence of MariaDB vectors," he says. "Like, if you ask a random LLM, 'What database should I use for vectors?' And you do not mention MariaDB; today, based on the training that the LLM models have right now, nobody suggests MariaDB." In one decidedly unscientific check, we asked Claude which database to use for vector search. It suggested PostgreSQL first and did not mention MariaDB. When asked to compare MariaDB with PostgreSQL for the same task, however, it had plenty to say. The tool knew about MariaDB's capabilities; it just didn't volunteer them. "I compare this to the old days of how to improve your Google ranking. It was sort of a mystical science. You did not really know how Google prioritized results. "Now the world has moved on [from search engine optimization] to LLM optimization." Arnö acknowledges that vendors could try to game the recommendations, but says: "I think the only proper way of influencing it is by having it and by documenting it and by people using it." That leaves MariaDB with a chicken-and-egg problem: without users generating examples and discussions of its vector search, AI tools have less material from which to learn about it. "The early movers have an undue advantage, and it's like if the water starts flowing in a certain direction, it will continue to flow in that direction. And now we have to change that and make people aware of what we are doing." MariaDB's efforts to attract developers also raise a question about which capabilities will remain available in its community edition. Galera, the clustering technology used with MariaDB, has attracted controversy over its open source future and its place in the company's enterprise product line. "You can have different opinions on whether that is exactly part of MariaDB, the core server, or not, but it is a product that was not part of MariaDB's core engineering team to begin with. It was managed by an entity that was acquired by MariaDB plc, which is a commercial entity and which is not equal to MariaDB server, and they are allowed to do whatever they want with it," Arnö says. "It's their freedom. It's their prerogative to decide what they want to do. What we protect is MariaDB server, and if anybody is messing with that, we would be quite upset!" ®
cd32e55b6f964e96: This week, world leaders descended on Manhattan for the UN General Assembly. It’s also New York Climate Week—investors, policymakers, advocates, and journalists are colliding at panels, talks, and fancy dinners.
With so many climate voices in one place, the discourse can feel a little louder than usual. This year, the unavoidable topic is artificial intelligence.

There’s been a growing tension bubbling up about AI’s impacts on climate and climate tech. Depending on where you stand, you might point to AI’s potential for advancing research, or to the way funding and attention from Big Tech is trickling into energy startups. Or you might focus on the emissions-heavy natural-gas buildout that’s unfolding to meet the sector’s electricity demand.

Everyone seems to agree that AI is important. The big question for those in the climate world, and the conversation I’m constantly having and hearing this week, involves how you see its influence unfolding.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres highlighted the AI and climate crossover in a speech on the first day of the assembly. “The climate crisis fuels instability and displacement,” Guterres said. “Artificial intelligence could help solve all these challenges, or it could make them worse.”

It feels relevant that this year is the first that the world has really had to grapple with the fact that climate goals are slipping out of reach. A recent report from the UN Environment Program said that the world has nearly passed the point where we could possibly keep warming to less than 1.5 °C above preindustrial levels.

Since we’ve essentially missed this target, the report lays out the need not only to quickly and drastically reduce greenhouse-gas emissions, but also to employ carbon removal to help suck up emissions that have already been released into the atmosphere.
The billion-dollar question is whether AI could help with any of this.

The energy-intensive technology is certainly shining a spotlight on the need to build out electricity supplies and shore up grid reliability. The result is more attention and money for energy technologies, some of which happen to be low- or zero-emissions.

As I’ve covered before, startups across the energy and climate sectors are benefiting. Firms in nuclear, geothermal, wind, and solar power have signed deals with the likes of Google, Meta, and others looking to power their new or growing data centers.

Global climate-tech investment from venture capital hit $26 billion in the first half of 2026, according to data from Currence, a finance tracker for the industry. That’s 55% higher than last year, and products and services for data centers are getting a massive slice of that pie.

But as a Semafor piece about the report points out, some sectors are slipping through the cracks: Carbon management and low-carbon fuels saw VC investment plummet this year. These are important solutions for addressing climate change but may not be able to sell themselves to a data center.

So far, the data center buildout has come with a hefty emissions toll. A few years ago, Microsoft, Google, and Meta all had ambitious goals to reduce greenhouse-gas emissions. Now they’ve all seen emissions rise, largely because of data centers that are needed to power AI.

Some people are optimistic. AI could help speed up progress in areas like the search for new catalysts, as Evelyn Wang, MIT’s VP of energy and climate, pointed out during a panel. And data centers won’t add to climate and water problems forever, Wang told the Associated Press. (She puts the timeline at about a decade until data centers no longer add to planet-warming emissions.)
But a whole lot of natural gas is coming online to meet the immediate demand created by new data centers. And once those power plants are built, they have a decades-long lifetime.

That’s partly why public pushback to AI is growing—people are seeing more pollution and noise near these data centers and the power plants that provide them with electricity. Overall, what I’m hearing this week is that many in the climate sector are skeptical of AI, at best.

“AI leaders are now on thin ice when it comes to license to operate and sinking deep underwater when it comes to public support,” said UN climate chief Simon Stiell in a speech this week. “Tech titans need to start showing why the benefits of AI outweigh its skyrocketing costs—for the many, not just the tiny few.”
This article is from The Spark, MIT Technology Review’s weekly climate newsletter. To receive it in your inbox every Wednesday, sign up here.
b10d9fae05301015: KUALA LUMPUR: Syahadat Ramli and Virandeep Singh made 68 runs to help Malaysia beat Hong Kong by eight wickets in the Asian Games men's Group B cricket match at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin on Thursday.
Hong Kong, ranked 24th to Malaysia's 25th in T20 international rankings, scored 81 runs for the loss of nine wickets before Malaysia ran down the target with 84 for two in 12 overs.
Captain Syed Aziz Mubarak and Haziq Aiman went to bat first but both managed just six runs before being bowled out.
But Syahadat and Virandeep shouldered Malaysia's charge by making 36 and 32 runs respectively for an impressive win.
Syahadat stroked three fours and two sixes while Virandeep had two fours and two sixes.
Bowlers Amir Azim Shukor and Pavandeep Singh took three wickets each.
With the win, Malaysia have virtually secured a place in the quarter-finals with a game to play against Oman on Saturday.
Syed Aziz said it was tough to play due to cracks on the cricket pitch.
"Credit to our bowlers, who did really well to restrict Hong Kong to 81 runs," said Syed Aziz.
"Our batters are also in good form to get the runs. It was a good team effort.
"In the Asian Games qualifier in Singapore last year, we lost to Hong Kong but we beat Oman for the Asian Games.
"Although we beat Hong Kong today, we have to wait for the outcome of the Oman-Hong Kong match tomorrow. If Oman beats Hong Kong, then we will finish top two to qualify for the quarter-finals.
"We will go all out to beat Oman to top the group and face Bangladesh in the quarter-finals. If we finish second in the group, then we will face Pakistan in the last four."

57a5572ea97a813d: KUALA LUMPUR: For seven years, retiree Mohd Nazli Ahmad Mahyadin was unable to fully enjoy the safety and comfort of his home as stray golf balls repeatedly landed in his compound.
The balls, hit from the neighbouring Darulaman golf course, cracked roof tiles, damaged a poultry coop, struck exterior walls and shattered a glass window.
The problem became so persistent that the 61-year-old lodged about 16 police reports between 2019 and January this year and repeatedly complained to the golf club.
Nazli can now hope for some peace after the High Court in Alor Star ruled that the golf course operator and landowner had subjected him to private nuisance.
Judicial commissioner Datuk Mohd Aimi Zaini Mohd Azhar ordered BDB Darulaman Golf & Resort Bhd and BDB Land Sdn Bhd to jointly pay Nazli RM100,000 in general damages and RM20,000 in costs.

"For nearly seven years, stray golf balls from the adjoining fairway turned a retiree's home into a hazard zone, forcing the plaintiff and his family to live defensively within their own residence," Aimi said in his grounds of judgment published by the Judiciary Department yesterday.
The judge said the evidence showed the incidents were not isolated but had continued for several years despite complaints and safety measures taken by the defendants.
Nazli owns and lives in a bungalow in Suasana Indah, Bandar Darulaman, Jitra, near Hole 7 of the golf course.
He bought the property from BDB Land in December 2004 and moved into the house on Dec 25, 2018.
According to the judgment, golf balls began landing in his compound almost immediately after he moved in.
Besides the police reports, Nazli produced photographs, WhatsApp messages and complaints made to the local authority. Seven neighbours also testified about similar incidents.
The court said Nazli's evidence was supported by contemporaneous documents and testimony from his neighbours.
It also rejected the defendants' suggestion that birds could have caused some of the roof damage.
"As for the suggestion that birds damaged the roof tiles, it remains a purely speculative theory unsupported by a single shred of evidence," Aimi said.
While dismissing Nazli's claim for trespass, the court found that private nuisance had been overwhelmingly established.
Aimi said the balls were hit by individual golfers and not directly by the defendants or their agents, meaning the requirement for trespass was not met.
However, he said the repeated intrusions went beyond an occasional inconvenience.
"The invasion was not an isolated or passing inconvenience; it was a persistent, multi-year state of affairs.
"Operating a golf fairway immediately adjacent to a residential boundary carries an obvious, foreseeable risk of off-target shots entering private yards," he said.
Aimi said the measures taken by the defendants were inadequate, resulting in "a severe, continuous, and unreasonable interference" with Nazli's residential life.
The court also found BDB Land liable despite its contention that it was merely the landowner and had no role in the golf course's daily operations.

Apart from being the registered owner of the golf course land, BDB Land was also the immediate holding company of BDB Darulaman Golf & Resort and had been involved in discussions on upgrading the safety netting.
Nazli's claims for special, exemplary and aggravated damages were dismissed.
Both defendants were also ordered to take remedial measures within 60 days.

These include raising and extending the safety netting near Hole 7, reviewing and, if necessary, repositioning the tee markers and line of play, installing safety warning signs and taking any further measures necessary to prevent golf balls from entering Nazli's property.

238bc6d5a5f8ca51: HANGZHOU: Malaysia secured potential investments exceeding RM28 billion following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou, which concluded today.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the potential investments were secured through engagements with 26 companies, including five major Chinese corporations.
"Through business roundtable sessions, prominent Chinese corporations focused on boosting investments in high-impact sectors capable of strengthening the country's industrial value chain.

"Key sectors identified with immense potential include semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, electric vehicles (EV), battery materials, advanced optics, biotechnology, health technology, medical devices, speciality chemicals and advanced manufacturing," he said at a press conference after officiating the Malaysia Pavilion at the fifth Global Digital Trade Expo (GDTE) here today.

Also present were Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, Transport Minister Anthony Loke and Malaysian Ambassador to China Datuk Norman Muhamad.
Anwar's visit also included Malaysia's participation in the 48th WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 and attendance at the GDTE.
He also held a bilateral meeting with Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers of the Kyrgyz Republic Akylbek Japarov.
Anwar said most of the companies expressed strong commitment to expanding their investments in Malaysia, driven by confidence in the government's stability and ongoing policy implementation.

"Business leaders are constantly observing geopolitical developments and bilateral relations. The friendly ties between Malaysia and China are currently on a very strong footing and progressing positively.
"Top Chinese leaders, including President Xi Jinping, Premier Li Qiang and cabinet ministers, have provided highly constructive encouragement and support for bilateral investments," he said.

He said the advanced medical sector held significant potential for deeper exploration, following rapid developments in China's medical technology, particularly AI applications and microsurgical procedures.

"I am deeply impressed by the medical technology advancements here, especially the application of AI and microsurgical procedures that have successfully restored sight for thousands of blind or visually impaired patients.
"This is a high-value sector that we should examine thoroughly to leverage cutting-edge technology for Malaysia's national development."
He added that environmental technologies, pollution control and meteorological research also offered broad opportunities for bilateral cooperation and investment.
2b76c39760b67044: KUALA LUMPUR: Tour bus operators are absorbing higher diesel costs for now, but the industry has warned the government it has at most two months before the financial strain forces operators to raise prices or leave the industry.

Malaysian Inbound Tourism Association (MITA) president Mint Leong Hoon Min said the unsubsidised diesel price – which had risen from RM5.27 per litre to RM5.42 per litre – had placed severe pressure on operator margins. She said members could sustain the current losses for no more than two months.
"Maximum is two months. If they keep raising the diesel price, the operators will get fed up and won't want to absorb the cost anymore.
"And when we raise our prices, the clients won't agree with us. Then they will stop selling tour packages to Malaysia, and we will lose the tourists," she told the New Straits Times.
Mint said the problem was not just the higher cost, but the unpredictability of weekly fuel price adjustments, making it difficult for operators to quote stable prices to foreign partners.
"When prices fluctuate, it is very difficult to promote our packages. Overseas clients might choose other destinations."
She said the situation was particularly acute for group tour operators, many of whom had signed contracts with overseas partners months in advance and could not pass on cost increases mid-contract.
"Some of them cannot pass the cost to the client. So they have no choice, they have to absorb the cost," she said.
She also pushed back against the notion that fuel price hikes would not affect tourism numbers, arguing that the damage would fall on operators rather than tourists directly.
She said individual travellers may still access subsidised e-hailing services and hop-on-hop-off buses, leaving tour bus operators unable to compete on price.
"The higher fuel charges will not kill the tourists, but will kill the players. The players now are absorbing the cost.
"When they cannot absorb it anymore, they will just leave the industry. Maybe the country will still get tourists to come, but the players are going to die," she said.
Mint said the industry had repeatedly approached the government for a diesel subsidy for tourism vehicles, but had been unable to qualify under existing subsidy schemes.
She estimated that fewer than 5,000 tourism vehicles were in operation nationally – a small enough number, she said, to make targeted subsidies feasible.
"We really hope the government can come up with other ways to subsidise if fuel subsidy is not possible," she said.

Peninsular Malaysia Tour Bus Association secretary-general Tai Poh Kim said bookings had already dropped, with domestic travellers postponing or cancelling trips in anticipation of higher transportation costs.
He also disputed the notion that tour buses primarily served foreign visitors.

"Most of the passengers using tour buses are Malaysian, not foreigners. Tour buses not only carry foreign tourists – they also handle other local activities like weddings, cultural, religious, and sports events," he said, adding that the sector was the only one seriously affected by unsubsidised fuel prices.
856ecb5230963e7f: PETALING JAYA: Tengku Zafrul Aziz mengemukakan lima soalan kepada Menteri Besar Negeri Sembilan Ismail Lasim berhubung perubahan pendiriannya dalam isu proklamasi penurunan takhta Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.

Penasihat kanan politik perdana menteri berkata, kenyataan tujuh halaman Ismail hari ini banyak menyentuh bidang kuasa dan Perlembagaan tetapi masih gagal menjawab persoalan asas mengenai pendirian menteri besar itu sendiri.
Katanya, Ismail sebelum ini mendakwa dipaksa menandatangani dokumen berkaitan kedudukan raja, membuat laporan polis mengenainya serta menyatakan sokongan dan taat setia kepada Tuanku Muhriz.
“Tidak sampai 10 hari kemudian, kerajaan yang dipengerusikannya mengesahkan proklamasi itu dan meminta proses pewartaannya diteruskan,” katanya di Facebook.
Tengku Zafrul mempersoalkan sama ada Ismail benar-benar dipaksa menandatangani proklamasi pada 3 Ogos lalu dan, jika benar, siapa yang bertanggungjawab.
Beliau turut meminta penjelasan mengapa mesyuarat exco pada 15 Sept mengesahkan proklamasi itu, sedangkan Ismail membuat laporan polis pada 9 Sept dengan mendakwa beliau dipaksa.
Selain itu, Tengku Zafrul mempersoalkan faktor menyebabkan perubahan pendirian Ismail, sama ada beliau sekali lagi berdepan paksaan dan siapa yang ditemuinya dalam tempoh kritikal berkenaan.
Tengku Zafrul berkata, penjelasan Ismail kerajaan negeri tidak menentukan siapa yang menaiki atau meninggalkan takhta masih tidak menjawab persoalan mengenai perubahan pendirian beliau.
Terdahulu, Ismail berkata beliau dan bekas exco tidak membuat keputusan untuk menurunkan atau melantik Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan.

Ismial berkata, beliau dan barisan bekas exco juga tidak akan mencampuri siasatan, pertimbangan adat atau proses pemilihan yang terletak dalam bidang kuasa pihak ditentukan mengikut Undang-Undang Tubuh Kerajaan Negeri Sembilan 1959.

6c85f785bd96eb89: KENINGAU: A man was charged in the magistrate's court with murdering his mother in Tambunan, Sabah.
The accused, Elekson Langak, 31, who appeared before magistrate Flavian Edward Henry, understood the charge read to him, but no plea was recorded.
His plea will be taken at the High Court once the case is transferred there.
According to the charge, Elekson was accused of murdering the 56-year-old victim at about 2pm on Sept 11 at a rented house in Kampung Katagayan, Tambunan.

He was charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries either the death sentence or jail for a term of 30 to 40 years and, if not sentenced to death, a minimum of 12 strokes of the rotan upon conviction.
No bail was granted, and Elekson was remanded under Section 259 of the Criminal Procedure Code pending the disposal of the case.
The court fixed Oct 29 for further mention.
Prosecuting officer assistant superintendent of police Daniel Dominic prosecuted, while Elekson was unrepresented.

On Sept 12, the media reported that a man had been arrested on suspicion of murdering his mother, who was found dead with injuries caused by a sharp weapon at a rented house in Kampung Katagayan the previous day.

9a457e4477c8f746: KUALA LUMPUR: Permodalan Nasional Bhd's (PNB) increasingly diversified investment portfolio is helping cushion returns against geopolitical shocks, with over 30 per cent of its portfolio now invested overseas, its chief said.

PNB president and group chief executive Datuk Rizal Rickman Ramli said the portfolio had become more diversified across markets and asset classes, allowing stronger-performing investments to offset weaker returns during periods of volatility.
This was particularly important amid the latest tensions in the Middle East, following tariff-related uncertainties last year.
"We are always monitoring and rebalancing when there are opportunities," he said during a visit to Media Prima Bhd here today.
Rizal said PNB's overseas exposure had increased significantly from about a decade ago, when more than 98 per cent of its portfolio was invested in Malaysia.
The portfolio is now diversified across public and private markets, real estate and fixed income, among other asset classes.

PNB invests across Asia Pacific, Europe and North America, covering both developed and emerging markets. Its international equity portfolio includes individual stocks as well as global exchange-traded funds.
"If one asset class is unable to deliver competitive returns, another asset class can help to improve the overall portfolio," he said.
He said PNB would continue to rebalance its portfolio according to market conditions, citing fixed income as an example of an asset class that could come under pressure when interest rates rise.
Rizal also said media remained important to PNB, both as part of its investment portfolio and as a channel to reach Malaysians, particularly younger generations.
He said younger consumers were increasingly consuming information across multiple platforms rather than through a single media channel.

"For the next generation, we want them to know Amanah Saham Nasional Bhd and our products, not only Amanah Saham Bumiputera and Amanah Saham Malaysia, which many are already familiar with, but also variable-price funds, Hibah Amanah, zakat and takaful products," he said.
He said these products formed part of PNB's efforts to build more inclusive and comprehensive financial solutions for Malaysians.
2826c9e1e25de96d: JAKARTA: Don't think about the final yet, Bangladesh comes first.
That was the clear message from Harimau Malaya interim head coach Tan Cheng Hoe ahead of their FIFA Asean Cup opening clash against Bangladesh at Gelora Bung Karno on Friday.
Cheng Hoe stressed that his squad's focus is solely on Bangladesh, acknowledging that the opening match of any tournament comes with its own set of challenges.

He also wants his players to use the target set by newly appointed FA of Malaysia president Datuk Ab Ghani Hassan, who expects Harimau Malaya to reach the final, as motivation to kick off their campaign on a positive note.
"Yes, of course, we see it as a challenge, and at the same time, we are fully focused on this first game. As I've mentioned before, in any tournament, the first match is always difficult.
"We take the new president's target as a challenge. At the same time, I think our players are also very excited to participate in this inaugural FIFA Asean Cup.

"Naturally, in football, every match and every point is crucial. So it is very important for us to start with a good result against Bangladesh tomorrow," he said during the pre-match press conference.
Meanwhile, Cheng Hoe said all 23 players in camp are fit and available for selection, giving him plenty of options to field his best starting lineup for the opener.
He added that despite the relatively short preparation period, the Harimau Malaya squad remains well prepared, even after late adjustments had to be made to the original roster.
"Yes, all 23 players are ready for tomorrow's match. We are very happy to be together. Everyone is prepared.
"At the same time, having named the 23-man squad earlier, unfortunately over the last few days we had to replace three players," he said.
Harimau Malaya will kick off their campaign against Bangladesh at Gelora Bung Karno before taking on Indonesia at the same venue three days later.
Their final group fixture will see Malaysia face Singapore at the Si Jalak Harupat Stadium in Bandung on October 1, while the final is scheduled for Gelora Bung Karno on Oct 5.
84e473afadb0db1e: HANGZHOU, Sept 24 — Malaysia has secured more than RM28 billion in potential investments following trade talks with major Chinese industry players, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

2d2967daf387cc2f: JAKARTA, Sept 24 — An Indonesian appeals court cut the corruption sentence of Nadiem Makarim today by a year, but the tech founder vowed to have the Supreme Court quash his conviction entirely.
Nadiem, the co-founder of ride-hailing app Gojek and a former education minister, was sentenced to 10 years in June for graft tied to procurement of laptops for schools during the pandemic.

An appeals court in the capital Jakarta reduced his sentence to nine years and cut the amount of restitution Nadiem must pay from 809 billion rupiah (RM184 million) to 549 billion rupiah (RM125 million).
Nadiem, who is seeking to have his conviction overturned, told media after the ruling that he would take his case to the Supreme Court.
“We will immediately file an appeal as soon as possible,” Nadiem said.
“I will not give up, and I will not receive any result other than acquittal.”
Nadiem, a 42-year-old Ivy League graduate, quit Gojek to become one of Indonesia’s youngest cabinet members in 2019, and served as education minister until 2024.

He was found guilty of corruption and abuse of authority by changing tender requirements to favour the purchase of Google Chromebooks for schools to aid remote learning during Covid-19, resulting in around US$120 million in state losses.
Prosecutors argued that Nadiem’s acts were linked to Google’s investment in Gojek.
The appeals court upheld the lower court’s decision to hand him a separate one-billion-rupiah fine. Nadiem faces an additional prison term if he does not comply with the financial penalties.
Google was not charged in the case, and the company has denied any wrongdoing.
GoTo Group, created in 2021 after a merger of Gojek and e-commerce platform Tokopedia, said Nadiem had no decision-making role since his resignation from the company in 2019. — AFP
049498facdb13e0d: LONDON, Sept 24 — Taylor Swift yesterday announced she is releasing an expanded version of her album The Life Of A Showgirl with four new songs, reported PA Media/dpa.
The singer, 36, revealed the new tracks were written after it became the fastest-selling album in United States (US) history in its first week, with four million equivalent units sold.
Swift travelled to Sweden to celebrate the record with music producers Max Martin and Shellback, whose real name is Karl Schuster, and recorded the songs there.
She said in a statement: “About a year ago, you guys did a truly unfathomable thing.
“Something that completely blew my mind… You gave The Life Of A Showgirl the biggest first week for an album in history.
“I took a trip to Sweden to celebrate with Max and Shellback, my two collaborators on this album.
“Really, we just wanted to reflect and take in how grateful we were for the moment we were in, but there was a studio there, and we did what we do when we feel anything at all: We wrote more songs.
“I hope you love them, because they were born out of pure gratitude for your exuberance for and celebration of the album we made.
“The Life Of A Showgirl: The Encore, including four new songs, is out on Friday and available to pre-order and save now.”
The Life Of A Showgirl, released in October 2025, is Swift’s 12th studio album and was recorded during the European leg of her Eras Tour in 2024. It was the global bestselling album of 2025.
Her previous album, The Tortured Poets Department, was the bestselling album of 2024.
It comes after Swift announced the release of a new single, Patient Zero, on Tuesday.
Swift revealed the new track will be available on Friday and shared the cover art, which featured the singer leaning against a wall wearing a black high-neck, sleeveless top.
The track is Swift’s first release since she married NFL star Travis Kelce at New York City’s Madison Square Garden in July. — Bernama-PA Media/dpa

d0e94cff8ea43df3: PETALING JAYA: Deputy prime minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has defended the Registrar of Societies' (RoS) decision to suspend Perikatan Nasional (PN), saying it was not done arbitrarily, but based on complaints received.

Zahid, who is also Barisan Nasional chairman, said he hoped PN and its component parties would respond calmly to the suspension, particularly as the Melaka election is approaching.

Earlier today, RoS said the suspension followed a notice issued to PN on Tuesday seeking an explanation regarding a complaint lodged by Bersatu.

cc291d5e9e50f8bc: SAP experts are questioning whether a recent Salesforce public demo of its AI technology would breach the German vendor’s controversial API policy - launched in April - in production environments. Salesforce has denied it would break any of SAP’s access rules. During the keynote presentation at the CRM vendor’s flagship Dreamforce conference in San Francisco last week, Katie O'Neil, Salesforce product marketing director, showed how a Salesforce AI agent was able to perform supplier onboarding with SAP, showcasing global engineering manufacturer Siemens as a customer. The demo appears to show AI agent Marshall working in an SAP sandbox, learning “where to click, which fields are required,” O'Neil said. The AI agent would use “LLM reasoning to really understand the business rules behind that process,” she said. The outcome is that users working in Salesforce’s collaboration platform, Slack, can onboard customers in SAP, or so the demo purports to show. “Marshall will package them up, create a library of trusted actions, and that is where AI reasoning becomes deterministic execution. What does that mean? It means when it comes time for something like supplier onboarding, Marshall's not just improvising. Marshall is executing against the same set of trusted actions every single time, so you know you can rely on him,” O’Neil said. How ERP giant SAP — a company also betting its future on AI — feels about all this is another matter. Being demoted to providing backend systems while Salesforce takes control of the user experience is not part of the German vendor's plans, we assume. In a social media post, an independent SAP consultant argued that the demo, if replicated in the real world, would not be allowed by SAP under its API Policy. Mario de Felipe, VP SAP data and AI at IT and managed services company Apiphani, said the API policy forbids "impersonation techniques." At the same time, any autonomous AI must go through SAP "endorsed architectures" to get inside SAP applications. “Not only did they connect to the SAP API to update a supplier, which would have been simple, but not the wow-effect required for a keynote, they connected to an SAP system, captured SAP application logic… how the BP [business process] role model works... the complete SAP's product behavior,” he said. The demo was not the result of a new partnership between the vendors, he pointed out on LinkedIn. A Salesforce spokesperson told The Register: “There’s an important distinction here: the Dreamforce demonstration interacted with SAP through its user interface using service accounts, without using SAP APIs. The API-use restrictions cited in the LinkedIn post therefore do not apply to the activity demonstrated.” SAP has declined the opportunity to comment. Speaking to The Register, De Felipe pointed out SAP's API Policy prohibits API use for “interaction or integration with (semi-) autonomous or generative AI systems that plan, select, or execute sequences of API calls” unless “through and within the limits of SAP-endorsed architectures.” Scraping, harvesting, or systematic and/or large-scale data extraction or replication is also banned with the same caveat. “More than breaking the rules, Salesforce knew what they showed during that keynote is not what the customers should be doing," he claimed. "There is a way to do these things following SAP architecture: that's SAP's point of view. There is a way of doing these things following Salesforce architectures. But what Salesforce did is clearly [not] the best practice architecture on how to deploy AI agents.". Others see some rule-breaking in Salesforce’s demo. Marian Zeis, an independent SAP consultant in Germany, said he agreed with most of De Felipe’s interpretation. “Robotic Process Automation itself is generally fine. It gets more difficult once an LLM or autonomous agent starts planning and executing calls against SAP, because then SAP expects documented or endorsed access paths. I would not automatically call an agent acting with a user’s authorization an ‘impersonation technique.’ In the policy, that wording is used in the context of bypassing API controls, so it really depends on how the Salesforce demo is implemented,” he said. SAP's API Policy was launched in April, with some critics arguing it would prohibit the use of APIs to integrate with AI systems outside its endorsed architectures, locking out other systems users want to employ. “My bigger issue is the practical one: the API Policy is reasonable as a governance document, but it still does not fit very well with how customers actually work today,” Zeis said. In the LinkedIn comments to De Felipe's post, John Appleby, a long-time SAP expert and former CEO of SAP partner Avantra, cautioned that demos were often designed to “be edgy but not break any license agreements.” Whether the Salesforce demo broke any of the API policy rules was a grey area, he said, while there were also ways to integrate these kinds of technology through “a permissible layer like SAP Integration Suite.” “Given they are namedropping Siemens, you can be sure that this has been checked as compliant. But yeah, there have been dragons in this sort of use case ever since SAP's Indirect Access rules, which go back nearly two decades, and of course since the new API Policy was put in place,” he said. One senior analyst who spoke to The Register off the record said that SAP’s API policy was pure protectionism given how far the vendor is in any AI Race. Linking AI to RISE with SAP — the vendor’s partnership agreement to get customers to the cloud and upgrade their ERP software — was “a big mistake,” he said. SAP’s first effort at AI, called Joule, is only a digital assistant, he said. “The consequences of exclusivity is 93 percent — almost all large customers — are denied access, which explains why they have no significant case studies. SAP were forced to make some U-turns as their large customers are not going to RISE anytime soon,” he said. Later, SAP launched Joule Agent Builder, part of Joule Studio within SAP Build, which is accessible to all RISE and non-RISE customers. “This was released in December ’25 but they have not yet talked to anyone that has used it,” he said. Then in May, SAP began to offer AI to on-prem customers on legacy systems. “SAP API policy in April was to cover their announcement in the following month at Sapphire when announcing AI services for both ECC and S/4HANA on-prem,” he said. However, customers were not keen on “wasting money talking to their ERP” in the SAP-approved architectures, he said. Most SAP customers that have already deployed GenAI that used APIs will now be non-compliant according to the SAP API policy, he claimed. SAP would rather its customers built agents in its environment, and from there reached out to work with other systems. When it launched its Joule Studio 2.0 at its Sapphire conference in May, SAP said it would allow developers to create and manage AI agents which connect and collaborate with third-party tools and third-party agents. "We've made extensibility a core design principle… This allows you to connect them to your non-SAP applications, because we know you're going to have to do that," Muhammad Alam, SAP executive board member for product and engineering, said at the time. Whether this will be enough to prevent others — Salesforce, ServiceNow, Microsoft or whoever has the most natural fit with end users — from stealing a march on SAP is unanswered. Publishing an API policy document seems unlikely to stop them. ®

1f87f8f2371a5146: OSLO: Norway's central bank raised its policy interest rate by 25 basis points to 4.50% on Thursday, seeking to contain inflation, as expected by a narrow majority of analysts in a Reuters poll, and said it may hike again.

"It will likely be necessary to keep the policy rate elevated for a time, and the committee is prepared to raise the policy rate further if needed to bring inflation down to the 2% target within a reasonable time horizon," Norges Bank governor Ida Wolden Bache said in a statement.
The Norwegian crown strengthened to 10.76 against the euro at 8.06am, from 10.79am just before the announcement.

Norway's central bank raised rates by 25 basis points in May, moving sooner than most analysts had expected, but said in August that the future path of monetary policy would "depend on economic developments", casting some doubt on the way forward.
Among the 28 economists in the Sept 17-21 poll, 16 expected Norges Bank to announce a 25 basis-point hike to 4.50% on Thursday, while 12 predicted no change at this time.
A further seven economists predicted that a hike to 4.50% would come in the fourth quarter, and the vast majority of the economists polled predicted 4.50% to be the peak borrowing cost.
The Nordic country's core inflation rose to 3.0% year-on-year in August, below Norges Bank's official forecast of 3.3% for the 12-month period but still remaining above the central bank's target.
"Over the summer, underlying inflation moderated and was lower than expected.
"But the inflation outlook somewhat further ahead does not appear to have changed materially," Bache said in the statement.
1f760a7a45209245: KUALA LUMPUR: China continued to tighten their grip on the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games medal standings on Thursday, opening a 54-gold lead over hosts Japan, while Malaysia slipped to ninth.

c7eb492c5827b745: SINGAPORE, Sept 24 — A 37-year-old man has been jailed for 16 weeks after 71 cats were left in a Bukit Panjang public housing flat in severely unsanitary conditions for nearly two years, during which nine died.

According to CNA, Muhammad Khairul Naim Zainol was also barred from owning animals for 12 months after pleading guilty to 24 charges under Singapore’s Animals and Birds Act, with another 47 charges taken into consideration.
Khairul and his then-wife, Nurul Nadiah Noor Mohamed, had acquired several cats after buying the flat in 2018, but the unsterilised animals bred rapidly.
The couple moved out around April 2022, while electricity and water supplies to the unit were later cut over unpaid utility bills.

The cats’ condition came to light on February 20, 2024, after neighbours alerted authorities to a distressed cat on a third-floor air-conditioning ledge and complaints were made about an odour from the flat.
Animal and Veterinary Service officers and police later found 61 live cats, three decomposing carcasses, six cat skulls and skeletal remains belonging to at least six other cats inside.
Veterinary examinations found 44 of the surviving cats were thin or very thin and nine were severely emaciated, while many suffered dehydration, parasites, ear mites and respiratory problems.
Nurul Nadiah, who was also handed 71 charges when the pair were charged in May, has a separate case due to be heard on October 6.
7d28d9d4df1cc2fd: BEIJING: Residents in China's capital hope President Xi Jinping's high-stakes meeting with US counterpart Donald Trump in Washington will stabilise ties between the two countries, telling AFP on Thursday a trade war "hurts everyone".
Xi was greeted in Washington on Wednesday evening local time by Trump, kicking off a pomp-filled state visit where the two leaders are expected to discuss everything from AI and trade to Iran.
In Beijing, a 59-year-old resident surnamed Huang called it a "very important" visit which would be critical in shaping the relationship between the two global superpowers.

"As an ordinary citizen, I naturally hope that China-US relations can achieve long-term, stable, and mutually beneficial development," Huang told AFP in central Beijing on an overcast Thursday morning.
"I also hope that through President Xi's visit to the US and friendly, harmonious, and goodwill communication with President Trump, we can develop bilateral relations," he added.
Beijingers AFP spoke to were hopeful Xi's meeting with Trump would ease trade pressures, which came to a head with a blistering tariff war in 2025, before a fragile truce was reached in October.

Though analysts expect the summit to be more about spectacle than substance, there was an early breakthrough on Wednesday, when Washington announced a two-month extension of the trade truce that was due to expire in November.
Finance worker Lu Hao said he was watching for any economic agreements following the talks, recounting how "distressed" he and his clients were during the trade war.
"I really hope this visit sends out positive signals and brings more good news to global stock markets," 27-year-old Lu told AFP.
"Because at the beginning (of the trade war), our stock market took the brunt of the impact right from the start," he said.
"It became clear that a trade war is a lose-lose situation."
Lucy Lu, who works in the foreign trade services industry, told AFP that it "hurts everyone" when major powers clash.
"For export businesses, certain goods have become really hard to ship out" as a result of higher tariffs, said the 43-year-old.
"I really hope countries can maintain a friendly approach to tariffs."
'Toe-to-toe'
Artificial intelligence is also likely to come up in the talks, as both countries strive for dominance in technology and robotics, while also mitigating growing fears that AI could wipe out humanity.
"In terms of AI... China now has the strength to go toe-to-toe with the US," Lucy Lu told AFP.
Competition may still "outweigh agreements", because at the end of the day, she said, "whichever country gains the upper hand in the field of AI down the road" will likely come out stronger.
However, AI competition "should be a healthy and rational one, rather than a malicious one", Huang told AFP.
He expects Xi to stand firm on hot topics like Taiwan, the self-ruled island that Beijing claims as its territory and has threatened to seize by force.
Taiwan has ramped up its defence spending in recent years, but remains reliant on US security support to deter Beijing.
"Our government has its bottom line. I hope the US will respect China's bottom line and its sense of historical identity," Huang added.

2a20abec8a89d9b4: KUALA LUMPUR: The motorcycle lane on the Federal Highway heading towards Klang, where several riders crashed at the same location, will be resurfaced and fitted with a 40kph speed sign.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the improvements would be carried out following initial action by the Public Works Department (PWD) at the site.
He said damaged sections of the road had been temporarily patched, while a "Kurangkan Laju" (Slow Down) sign had been installed as an immediate safety measure.
"Skid tests in dry and wet conditions were also conducted to verify the actual performance of the surface.
"Following this, improvement works, including milling and paving the road surface and installing a 40kph advisory speed sign, will be carried out," he said in a Facebook post today.
Nanta said preliminary information showed that the coloured surface on the motorcycle lane had been designed and applied as an anti-skid treatment in accordance with the specified work requirements.
However, it was drizzling at the time of the incidents and the road surface was reported to be slightly wet, with several motorcyclists crashing at the same location.
He said PWD had been instructed to conduct a comprehensive technical investigation without drawing any early conclusions on the cause of the incidents.

Among the aspects being examined are the surface's skid resistance when wet, the condition of the road surface, possible contamination by substances such as oil or diesel, and the quality of the work carried out.
The investigation will also consider other factors that may have contributed to the incidents.
"What is important is that we learn from this incident.
"If the investigation finds weaknesses in the materials, workmanship, design or maintenance, we will take appropriate corrective action," he said.
Nanta also expressed sympathy to the motorcyclists involved and stressed that the safety of road users who use the lane daily remained a priority.
A 42-second video went viral on social media yesterday showing several motorcycles lying on the Federal Highway motorcycle lane, with several riders seen by the roadside.
The video also showed the coloured lane appearing wet, while other motorcyclists slowed down when passing through the area.
The post claimed the incidents occurred during rain and that similar incidents had happened twice.
In August, PWD said the coloured surface at the Subang exit was a localised surface treatment implemented based on engineering considerations and with the approval of the relevant authorities.
It said the coloured surface was intended to mark areas with a higher risk of conflict, such as bends and exit lanes, while reminding motorcyclists to exercise greater caution.

77560c0c7df146c6: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — In a double courtroom defeat for rail contractor Emrail Sdn Bhd, the High Court has dismissed its RM59.1 million lawsuit against Kuwait Finance House (M) Bhd (KFH) and ordered the company alongside three personal guarantors to pay the bank RM39.09 million.

Justice Quay Chew Soon dismissed Emrail's claim over a disputed performance bond for the Light Rail Transit 3 (LRT3) development in its entirety and allowed KFH’s counterclaim in full, holding the contractor and its guarantors jointly and severally liable for the outstanding debt, FMT reported.
The three personal guarantors ordered to satisfy the judgment debt are prominent corporate figures Zaki Azmi, Hari Narayanan Govindasamy, and his son, Amrish.

The litigation turned on whether KFH was contractually bound to issue a performance bond conforming strictly to the template prescribed by MRCB George Kent Sdn Bhd (MRCBGK), the project delivery partner (PDP) for the LRT3 project.
“The central question underlying the plaintiffs’ claim is not what the employer wanted, but what the defendant (KFH) agreed to do,” Quay ruled in his judgment issued today.

The judge held that the underlying Islamic financing facility expressly stipulated that the Kafalah bank guarantee had to be in a form, and addressed to parties, acceptable to KFH. This contractual term gave KFH unfettered discretion to decide whether the wording and structure of the requested bond were acceptable.
The court further established that the specific performance bond template required by Emrail was never incorporated into the financing agreement with KFH.
Quay ruled that Emrail could not rely on its independent construction contract with MRCBGK to enforce obligations against KFH, which was not a party to that agreement.
“The plaintiffs have conflated Emrail’s contract with its employer/PDP and its financing contract with the defendant,” he said.

The court also rejected Emrail’s argument that KFH had acted negligently by failing to issue a compliant bond, ruling that a claimant cannot use the tort of negligence to extract a more favourable commercial bargain than what was negotiated under contract.

On Emrail’s claim that the lack of a compliant bond caused RM59.1 million in interim project payments to be withheld, the judge found that the contractor failed to establish causation. The court noted that Emrail offered no proof that MRCBGK would have certified or released the sums, observing that other LRT3 contractors faced industry-wide payment arrears, with Emrail itself eventually receiving around RM402.5 million under a subsequent contract for the rail project.
Ruling on KFH’s counterclaim, Quay held that the financing facility expired on Oct 31, 2021, leaving an outstanding debt of RM39,089,705.42 as of May 16, 2025.

The court ordered Emrail and the guarantors to settle the sum within one month, alongside post-judgment interest at 5 per cent per annum from the date of the decision until full settlement, and awarded KFH RM100,000 in legal costs.
Lawyers S. Shaarvin Raaj, A. Anusha, K. Ravvenneah, J. Jeyakrishna, and Iman Nur Alya represented Emrail and the guarantors.
Counsel Syed Faisal Al-Edros Syed Abdullah, Mohd Wafiy Azman, Choo Shi Jin, Nasbal Harun, Ahmad Iqbal Rohaizan, and Wardah Yunus acted for KFH.
bcc6465c58a414c8: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is laying the foundations for broader economic activity through digital assets, although their full potential will depend on how the technology and ecosystem scale, says the Securities Commission (SC).
SC digital strategy and innovation executive director Dr Wong Huey Ching said digital assets were already contributing to economic activity, although their longer-term potential remained uncertain.
She said the presence of companies and firms operating in Malaysia and employing people in the digital asset space was encouraging from an economic growth perspective.
"I think there is economic activity. Whether or not it fully realises the potential is something that we don't know," she said.
Wong was responding to a question during a fireside chat at the Luno Institutional Digital Asset Conference 2026, themed "The Next Chapter: Malaysia's Evolving Digital Asset Regulatory Framework."
Wong said SC saw potential for digital assets and blockchain-based solutions to address issues in the capital market.
She said there were still many unknowns, including varying levels of familiarity with the technology and whether it could scale effectively.
She added that SC was closely monitoring how the technology could scale, citing evidence from selected markets while assessing how such applications could be applied in Malaysia.
Meanwhile, Luno Malaysia country manager Scarlett Chai said regulated digital asset trading should be viewed as part of the economic foundation needed for the ecosystem to develop.
She said trading value on regulated digital asset exchanges (DAXs) rose 23 per cent to RM17.14 billion in 2025, from RM13.93 billion in 2024.
"A well-regulated trading market lends confidence and liquidity for institutions to build and mature.
"At the end of the day, you don't get tokenised bonds or stablecoin settlement without a trusted market underpinning everything," she added.

Chai said regulatory developments were also strengthening the foundations of the digital asset ecosystem, including stronger client asset safeguards, financial stability requirements and management competency standards.
She said digital asset exchanges would also be brought formally into the Financial Markets Ombudsman Service under the SC's revised guidelines.
"In 2026 alone, we've seen multiple other tokenisation efforts across both TradFi (traditional finance) and digital asset ecosystems.
"The honest answer is that we are currently paving the foundations for greater, more robust economic activity, and the immediate two-to-three-year timeframe will demonstrate further potential.
"We would also start looking beyond trading volumes, and into tracking different indicators such as jobs created, institutional participation, or tokenised assets issued," she added.

Chai said Malaysia's regulatory approach also provided opportunities to attract companies building within the regulatory perimeter, including custody providers, tokenisation platforms, compliance and regulatory technology firms.
She said there was also an opportunity in Shariah-compliant digital finance, given Malaysia's established position in Islamic capital markets.
"The more of this infrastructure that's built and regulated locally, the more credible and productive the entire ecosystem becomes for investors, businesses, and the economy at-large," she said.
She noted that Malaysia's digital asset talent pipeline had also grown, although there remained tighter constraints for specialists in compliance and risk.
These specialists, she said, needed to understand both digital assets and Malaysian capital market regulations.
She said regulatory clarity and access to functioning sandboxes could be more valuable to serious digital asset companies than tax incentives alone.

"Malaysia doesn't need to compete on tax breaks alone. Regulatory clarity and functioning sandbox access, letting companies build and test without needing a full licence on day one, are worth more to serious builders.
"This is especially true for serious builders than a lower tax rate in a market with an uncertain rulebook.
"Continuing to invest in platforms for dialogue and closer university-industry alignment will do more for the long-term talent pipeline than incentives alone ever could," Chai added.

c19189d39791f641: KUALA LUMPUR: Veteran actor Azhar Sulaiman, 55, harbors no jealousy towards young actors commanding fees of up to RM100,000 for film projects, viewing it simply as a matter of individual fortune.
​Azhar said an actor's pay should not be a point of contention, as it depends on their credibility, commercial value, and ability to help make a production a success.

​"If an actor asks for RM100,000 and the producer is willing to pay it, then good luck to them. If the producer is confident that the actor can deliver a return on investment, why not?" he told Berita Harian.
​According to Azhar, high fees are justifiable if an actor has the pull to make a film a hit.
​"Even if he isn't a traditional actor—perhaps just a content creator—if his presence draws an audience and helps the film succeed, that's simply smart business," he said.
​Azhar noted that star status isn't measured solely by social media popularity or the number of awards won, but by audience acceptance and the ability to pull viewers into cinemas.
​"You can see true star quality in audience acceptance and an actor's growth over time. It isn't just about winning awards," he added.
​Grateful to have kicked off his acting career on the big screen, Azhar acknowledged that despite nearly four decades in the business, he still holds strong market value.

​"Film stars hold a distinct status in the industry. Back in my day, I started as a film star, too. That's why my market value remains secure to this day. If I had started out in small TV dramas, my rate might have dropped by now.
​"Those of us who started in films and stayed active have far more secure rates—we can still command around RM3,000 a day," he explained.
​Azhar also sees no reason to air his rates on social media just to gain attention or sympathy.

​"If I get a low offer, I'd never complain on social media or claim a production house is disrespecting me just because they offered RM500 a day. Likewise, if I were paid RM5,000 a day, I wouldn't go around boasting about how well I'm doing.
​"I simply do not—and never will—discuss my pay in public," he said.

1080109f56e8f82f: Shortcuts work against the rewards of friendship: authentic relationships can surely only be forged when you’re not expecting a return on your money What price would you put on friendship? 5c970d3c2fb65af6: TOKYO: Japanese teenager Shin Ohashi smashed the men's 200m breaststroke world record at the Asian Games on Thursday, setting a new mark of 2min 04.83sec.
The 17-year-old cut more than half a second off the previous mark of 2:05.48 held by China's Qin Haiyang.
Qin's record had stood since July 2023.
Ohashi had already won the 100m breaststroke gold this week in Tokyo after a dead heat with China's Dong Zhihao.
"My target has always been to break the world record and I'm so happy to have done it," said Ohashi.
"A lot happened before this competition but a lot of people helped me get to this point and I am very grateful to them.
Ohashi finished 3.84sec faster than silver medallist Denis Petrashov of Kyrgyzstan.
The Japanese teen took control from the off and from then it was a race against the clock.
He will now be the man to beat at the Los Angeles Olympics in two years' time.
"My next goal is to win gold at next year's world championships and then go on to win gold at the Olympics," he said.
"I don't want to be satisfied and I want to feel these emotions again."
Previous world record holder Qin did not swim the 200m at this year's Asian Games.-AFP
75127889ec07016d: NAGOYA: Defending champion Ng Eain Yow left no room for drama as he downed South Korea's Ryu Jeong Min to book his spot in the last eight of the squash men's singles event at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Thursday.
Eain Yow churned out a calculated 11-3, 11-4, 11-5 win over Jeong Min at the Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena to set up a quarter-final encounter with Hong Kong's Lau Tsz Kwan on Friday.
Eain Yow, the world No. 18, said he was pleased with how he executed his plans against Jeong Min, the world No. 184.
"I feel that my performance today was quite good because my opponent is technically very capable," he said.
"But I did what I had to and executed my tactics well. It was a good performance."
Eain Yow, who has never competed in Japan before, added that he is beginning to get more comfortable competing here.
"There are some small challenges playing here, but nothing major. We have to adapt to new conditions on tour every week," he said.
"The courts are a bit colder compared to other courts so the bounce is a bit lower. You just need a bit more time to adapt but I actually think it suits me better."
Eain Yow, who is in the top half of the draw, added that he is expecting a tough fight against Tsz Kwan, the world No.47.
"We are quite used to playing each other so I know what to expect. It will be a tough match," he said.
"But this week it is all about myself and focusing on what I need to do. I am not thinking too much about my opponents.
"If I can do what I need to do, I can win every match."
Sanjay Jeeva's campaign in the men's singles, however, came to an end.
Sanjay was pipped 11-9, 8-11, 11-6, 15-17, 11-6 by India's Veer Chotrani in a tough five-setter.
a5bf4fd78b0a9009: JAKARTA: An Indonesian court has reduced the prison sentence of Gojek founder and former education minister Nadiem Makarim to 9 years from 10 years in an appeal hearing for a graft conviction relating to improper laptop procurement, judges said on Thursday.

Nadiem was sentenced to 10 years in prison in June after the court found him guilty of abusing his authority during the procurement of Google Chromebooks for schools in Indonesia that led to $125 million in state losses.
He filed an appeal on July 1 to the Jakarta high court.

One judge, Catur Iriantoro, said on Thursday that they did not approve Nadiem's appeal to dismiss all charges because the previous ruling was consistent with the facts established at trial, the evidence presented, and witness testimony.
The court also cut the amount of restitution Nadiem must pay from 809 billion rupiah ($45.23 million) to 548 billion rupiah, another judge, Subachran Hardi Mulyana, said.
After the hearing, Nadiem expressed his disappointment about the ruling and told reporters he would file another appeal to the Supreme Court.
"The victim now is not just me, but the credibility of the law enforcement system in Indonesia," he said.
Judges also upheld a previous ruling that said Makarim had adjusted the tender requirements to favour Chrome, which benefited Google and restricted competition.

Nene Royal, whose real name is Rattikarn Amloy, took home the US$1 million (RM4.08 million) prize as winner of America’s Got Talent, after wowing judges with blistering guitar solos and rock ballad shrieks.
The teen from the island of Phuket has been a social media sensation in Thailand since entering the competition and was invited to play with Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in July.
Anutin, who is currently in New York for the UN General Assembly meetings, sent his congratulations to Nene, the first Thai national to win the hit TV show.
He praised her talent and dedication, which “brought pride to Thai people”, according to deputy government spokeswoman Ploythalay LaksameesaengJanuary
Nene, who says she started playing guitar at age seven, collapsed to the stage floor in California when her victory was announced.

Nene said she learned guitar mostly by watching online videos, and then got a music scholarship to the private international school.
“When I played the first chord, I fell in love and I thought — I am going to be the girl rock star,” she said in an interview with AGT.
The school said it knew from the beginning she was “an extraordinary talent with a bright future ahead”.
The Phuket night market where Nene cut her teeth also hailed her as an inspiration.

"Next to the accused's house is a car wash where three workers often used the toilet at the house. They had previously been arrested but were released on police bail.
"Based on the evidence of the prosecution witnesses, there was no information linking the second accused, Nurul Syahira, to the drugs found.

The prosecution was conducted by Deputy public prosecutor Nik Nur Adila Mat Zaidan.

d1f3baee16420714: KUALA LUMPUR: Mahkamah Tinggi menolak tuntutan RM59.1 juta oleh kontraktor rel Emrail Sdn Bhd terhadap Kuwait Finance House (M) Bhd (KFH) berhubung pertikaian bon pelaksanaan bagi projek LRT3.
Hakim Quay Chew Soon turut membenarkan tuntutan balas KFH dan memerintahkan Emrail bersama tiga penjamin membayar RM39.09 juta kepada bank itu secara bersama dan berasingan.
Ahli perniagaan Zaki Azmi, Hari Narayanan Govindasamy dan anaknya, Amrish, bertindak sebagai penjamin bagi kemudahan pembiayaan berkenaan.

Pertikaian utama dalam kes itu ialah sama ada KFH pernah bersetuju mengeluarkan bon pelaksanaan mengikut format yang ditetapkan MRCB George Kent Sdn Bhd (MRCBGK), selaku rakan penyampaian projek (PDP) LRT3.

“Persoalan utama yang menjadi asas tuntutan plaintif bukan mengenai apa yang dikehendaki pihak majikan, tetapi apa yang dipersetujui defendan (KFH) untuk dilakukan,” katanya dalam penghakiman setebal 63 muka surat yang disampaikan hari ini.

82d596295be30fbb: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 24 — The collaboration between the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) continues to be strengthened to combat the misuse of network services for the purpose of online child sexual exploitation.

Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said MCMC, as the technical agency, would continue to play an important role in assisting PDRM, especially the D11 Division (Sexual, Women and Child Investigation) of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), in tracking down those who misuse network services and subsequently bringing them to justice.

“The MCMC’s role is to ensure that anyone who misuses network services can be traced, arrested and brought to justice, especially those who prey on children and women,” he told Bernama and RTM after attending the Communications Ministry’s ‘Jasamu Dikenang’ (Appreciation) ceremony here today.
Fahmi said the collaboration also involved technical and forensic aspects to assist PDRM investigations into online child sexual exploitation activities.

Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said on Sept 22 that eight teenagers, including a 13-year-old, were among 53 individuals arrested for suspected involvement in activities related to child sexual abuse material (CSAM) under Op Pedo Integrated 3.0 conducted recently.

The suspects were detained in simultaneous operations conducted from Sept 14 to 16 following intelligence gathered by the CID’s D11 unit with the MCMC, with police also detecting activities involving the production, distribution and sale of CSAM-related videos and animations through closed online groups, with the material being offered for between RM50 and RM60.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said the MCMC was also placing emphasis on the safety aspects of social media platforms through the legal framework related to online safety.

“Through the Online Safety Act, we are also emphasising to social media platforms the need to ensure that the environment or platform itself remains safe, especially for women and children, notably those below the age of 16 are not allowed to open social media accounts,” he said.

Regarding the appreciation ceremony, which honoured 157 retirees and soon-to-retire employees from the Communications Ministry, Fahmi said the experience and insights of retired civil servants should continu to be utilsed to help improve government services, especially in the field of communications.
“I pray that they will continue to find ways to share their views and contribute to ensuring the government’s efforts, especially in the communications, remain successful in the eyes of the people.
“If there is anything they wish to share with us for improvement, I am very open to receiving their feedback,” he added. — Bernama
